# clipaste hardened fork

Canonical repository: https://github.com/dingdinglz/clipaste
Read README.md, SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md in that repository before installing.

This fork requires bearer authentication for clipboard type and image endpoints.
Only /health is public metadata. Tokens use OS randomness and private configuration
files. Never place tokens in command-line arguments, URLs, logs or chat messages.

Default CLIPASTE_SERVER_ONLY=1 leaves the local clipboard unchanged. Default
CLIPASTE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=3600 expires image caches after one hour. Zero retention
explicitly opts into indefinite storage. Cleanup occurs at startup and roughly
every minute while the daemon runs, not while stopped; deletion is not secure erasure.

Install the reviewed fork source using cargo install --path . --locked. There is
no advertised fork Homebrew tap or prebuilt binary release. Do not install upstream
Homebrew/releases and claim these protections. No login service is auto-installed.

Local clipboard host: run clipaste, then in another terminal run
clipaste ssh-setup user@host. Reconnect using the same destination. Linux remote
Claude Code uses Control+V, not Command+V. Codex and macOS remotes use
clipaste-paste and hand the resulting remote path to the agent.

WSL setup imports the Windows credential explicitly with --token-file PATH.
Keep token copies private (Unix0600) and use literal IP addresses for --host.
Do not expose the listener publicly as a networking workaround.

Only trusted remote accounts should receive credentials; root and same-account
processes are inside the trust boundary. One compromised configured account can
compromise the shared credential. Follow SECURITY.md for revocation/migration.

Do not run a daemon, touch the general clipboard, connect user servers or edit
real SSH configuration as a development test. Tests use temporary homes and named
pasteboards. Run cargo test --locked and strict Clippy, and verify cross-platform
CI before claiming cross-platform runtime coverage.
